critic_summary: The active method's empirical pre-check only validates that the targeted event class is non-empty in cached artifacts — it never measures the aggregate consequence of acting on that class, and it has no architectural-diversity guard. Loops 2, 3, and 4 all conditioned on the on-order quote tick with renamed predicates (wide spread skip, tight spread submit, in-flight unrealized-PnL override) and all lost vs base; the trace explicitly identifies the underlying anti-pattern as 'use the on-order quote tick to filter which flips to honor' and explicitly says a multi-candidate probe with structural-axis diversity would have caught it. The proposed method (kept-but-applied-on-revert reasoning) does four things: (1) reads prior NOTES.md and HARD-BANS conditioning axes already explored, (2) requires four candidates each on a different (object, temporal aspect) with a diversity check, (3) adversarially ranks by hardest-to-dismiss counterargument and runs the top TWO as real algorithms on one median-volume probe date with six pre-committed numbers, (4) tournament-gates with an explicit PROCEED-LESS-BAD escape valve so the loop always produces gate-comparable 12-date metrics rather than aborting (the loop-3 critic's escape-valve idea, retained). On a revert: the running best is loop-2, whose prompt_in was prompt-l1.md, so .current_prompt.md is restored to prompt-l1.md and the proposal sits at prompts/proposed/loop-4-proposal.md. If the proposal had been kept, the next reasoning trace should contain four distinct conditioning-axis labels, an explicit banned-axis list cross-referenced to prior loops, six pre-committed numbers across two probed candidates, an adversarial counterargument ranking, and a tournament-winner selection tied to a single-date PnL delta — not a single-candidate proposal extending the on-order-quote axis.
